articles.title: Right vs. Remedy: No Standing to Challenge the Patent Cover’s ‘Right to Exclude’ Promise
articles.content:
密歇根大学法学院教授丹尼斯·克鲁奇（Dennis Crouch）撰文指出，每一项颁发的专利都附带一项承诺，授予持有人在全美范围内排除他人制造、使用、出售或提供该发明的权利。然而，这一承诺在20年前因最高法院在《eBay公司诉MercExchange公司》案（547 U.S. 388，2006年）中的判决而变得误导。此后，法院开始拒绝在确认专利有效性和侵权后颁发禁止令来终止持续侵权行为。

一批发明者权益组织以行政程序法（APA）为依据，起诉美国专利商标局（USPTO），要求法院命令该机构修改其在每项专利封面上印制的语言。尽管未审理案件实体，但地区法院以缺乏诉讼资格为由驳回了诉讼。联邦巡回法院近日维持了这一驳回裁决（US Inventor, Inc. v. Squires, No. 24-2378 (Fed. Cir. Aug. 21, 2026)），由纽约东区法院法官科夫纳（Kovner）主笔判决书。

这是近一年来US Inventor第二次因诉讼资格问题在联邦巡回法院败诉。去年秋季，法院裁定该组织无资格挑战USPTO拒绝其提议的“小实体IPR抗辩权”规则。但本案更多是为了吸引公众对eBay案及其后续案件影响的关注，因为修改专利封面红丝带旁的语言不会产生法律影响。

无论该陈述是否存在误导性，法院发现每个原告均承认知晓eBay案对禁止令的影响，因此无人面临再次被误导的真实威胁。这意味着当事人并未面临持续损害——因为他们仅要求展望性救济（修改未来的语言）。无损害，即无诉讼资格。
articles.summary:
by Dennis Crouch

Every issued patent comes with a promise granting "to the person(s) having title to this patent the right to exclude others from making, using, offering for sale, or selling the invention throughout the United States of America . . ."  35 U.S.C. § 154(a)(1).  But, that sentence became misleading twenty years ago when the Supreme Court decided eBay Inc. v. MercExchange, L.L.C., 547 U.S. 388 (2006) and courts began refusing to award injunctive relief to stop ongoing infringement even after a finding of enforceability and infringement.

A group of inventor advocacy organizations sued the USPTO under the Administrative Procedure Act (APA), seeking a court order for the agency to rewrite the language that it places on the cover of each patent.  Without reaching the merits,  the district court dismissed the suit for lack of standing.  The Federal Circuit has now  affirmed that dismissal.  US Inventor, Inc. v. Squires, No. 24-2378 (Fed. Cir. Aug. 21, 2026).  Judge Kovner (E.D.N.Y., sitting by designation) wrote the opinion.

This is the second time in the past year that US Inventor has lost a Federal Circuit appeal on standing grounds. Last fall the court held that the group lacked standing to challenge the USPTO's denial of its petition for an IPR opt-out rule for small entities. Dennis Crouch, Who Gets to Challenge USPTO Rules? Federal Circuit Says Big Tech Yes, Small Inventors No, Patently-O (Oct. 3, 2025).  But this case is more about focusing attention on the impact of eBay and its progeny because the change in language next to the digital red ribbon would have no legal impact.

Regardless of whether the statement is misleading, the court found that each plaintiff admitted to knowing exactly what eBay did to injunctive relief, so none faces a real threat of being misled again.  That means there is no ongoing harm to the parties - since they asked only for prospective relief (change the language going forward).  No harm, no standing.
